entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
McDonald's Corporation is an American multinational fast-food corporation founded in 1940 by Richard and Maurice McDonald in San Bernardino, California, and franchised by Ray Kroc starting in 1955. It became the world's largest restaurant chain, serving over 69 million customers daily in 100+ countries, and defining the global fast-food industry.

The McDonald brothers' 'Speedee Service System' — applying assembly-line principles to food preparation — created the template for fast food. Ray Kroc's franchising vision transformed a regional burger stand into a global empire, with McDonald's pioneering the franchise business model now used across thousands of industries. The golden arches became one of the world's most recognized brand symbols, more widely recognized than the Christian cross in international surveys.

McDonald's expansion strategy tied to US military bases and suburban highway culture embedded it in American and global consumer life. Its Happy Meal, introduced in 1979, created a generation of brand-loyal customers. The company's labor practices, environmental impact, and role in obesity became central debates in public health and corporate responsibility. McDonald's influence shaped agriculture, supply chains, and urban planning through the 'McDonaldization' of society described by sociologist George Ritzer.
